title: Governed Agent Loop cursor
description: The single mutable record of loop position. The only loop file that lives outside the gate (GAL-D05). One file, one writer at a time (rule 6, the mutex), every timestamp from the host clock. Additional properties are permitted so a project can extend it; the fields here are the ones the protocol reads.

state.description: Where the loop is. 'dispatched' means exactly one job is in flight (GAL-D10). 'indeterminate' means a job passed its timeout plus grace without a terminal status and is parked, not running (GAL-D09). 'hold-pending' means harvest, review and gate ran and the merge is waiting on the operator.

current_packet.description: Packet id in flight, e.g. PKT-012. Null when idle.

job_id.description: The execution substrate's job identifier. The only handle used for liveness; never a pid.

worktree.description: Repo-relative worktree path for the agent, e.g. .worktrees/agent-PKT-012.

attempt.description: Increments on re-dispatch of the same packet (e.g. a fix1 attempt into the same worktree).

main.description: Local integration-branch tip as of the last tick.

origin_gap.description: From `git rev-list --left-right --count origin/<main>...<main>`. Written every tick. The publish at step 6d (GAL-D18) is what closes it; a non-zero ahead count after a tick means that publish was refused or skipped, and the refusal is recorded beside it.

merge_hold.description: Operator-set flag interposing between gate and merge. A held tick runs harvest, review and the full gate, then stops. Only the operator clears it; a repository change is evidence, never an instruction that clears a hold.

lock_history.description: Last ten lock acquisitions. The entry is written at step 1c immediately after acquisition with released_at null, so the cursor always names the current holder (GAL-D16); step 9a fills released_at BEFORE the ref is deleted, because deleting the ref deletes its reflog and the cursor is then the only in-tree evidence of ownership.

released_at.description: Null while the lock is held.

lock.description: Advisory mirror of the real mutex (the refs/pm/tick-lock git ref). Written by the holder at step 1 and nulled at step 9. The git ref is authoritative; this field exists so a re-read can detect ownership change without a git call.

job_id.description: The tick's own id, e.g. tick24-1825z.

queued.description: Dispatchable packets in order. One line each, including any sequencing condition.

parked.description: Items awaiting an operator decision, one line each with current status. The full text lives in the pending-decisions file on the integration branch.

dec_pending_inbox.description: Entries staged for carriage onto the next packet branch (GAL-D03). Drained by the supervisor at step 7. The staging area is the one place a ruling given in an attended session may legitimately originate (GAL-D07 scope clarification).

carriage.description: Where it lands, e.g. 'rides the next packet branch under the gate per GAL-D03'.

last_tick_result.description: One paragraph. What the last tick did, in the report order: new decisions, merges, dispatches, failures.

notes.description: Standing notes for future ticks. Protocol amendments owed, substrate quirks learned, operator instructions carried forward.

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 UTC, read from the host clock via a command. Never estimated. A forward-dated value suppresses legitimate ticks for the length of the skew.
